Done. The plan succeeded on its first and only execution.

**What the plan does** (`out/T3/plan.yaml`):

- Pre-checks that the input holds 244 tensors, 48 buffers and 64 projection matrices, so a bad pattern fails as a no-match instead of silently passing.
- Deletes the 48 buffers with a full-match regex on `attention.bias`, `attention.masked_bias` and `attention.rotary_emb.inv_freq`. Escaped dots keep the mask buffer separate from the `attention.dense.bias` parameter.
- Upcasts every remaining tensor to float32 in place, then downcasts exactly the 64 projection matrices to bfloat16.
- Asserts the required checks before writing: the projection regex matches 64 tensors and they are all bfloat16, every other tensor is float32 via a negative-lookahead regex, layer 0 query_key_value is bfloat16, the input embedding is float32, no buffer remains, and 196 tensors exist.
- Writes sharded safetensors to `out/T3` with a 256MB shard budget.

**Verified output**:

| Item | Result |
|---|---|
| Tensors in index | 196 (132 float32, 64 bfloat16) |
| Shards | 9, every name in the index maps to the shard holding it |
| Oversized tensors | the two 412 MB float32 embeddings, each alone in its own shard |
| Other shards | all at or under 256 MiB of tensor data |

The self-report is in `out/T3/REPORT.md`. One thing worth knowing for the study: the tool has no assert that counts tensors by dtype, so "exactly 64 bfloat16" had to be expressed as a count on the projection pattern plus a float32 check on its complement.
